clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: I wanted to prove that I belong. I am the sixth pick, I was the first guard taken in the draft. I wanted to prove that I belong. And so, that was the first mindset I had. And then when I got there, and we started training camp, and we had all these veterans. There was only two rookies on the team, and the rest of them were veterans. Most of them didn't want to practice. Most of them didn't even care about winning. There was a lot of strife between the best players, Jeff Petrie and Sidney Wicks, both great players.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on his mindset as a rookie in the NBA
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins recalls his rookie mindset in the NBA, noting that many veterans on his team were more focused on strife than winning games.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: I wanted to prove that I belong.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: We in the locker room and dude pulls out a cigarette, starts smoking in the locker room. And then somebody said, 'Man, let me get a light from your smokes.' Anybody, 'Yo, you got a smoke over there for me?' We got three or four guys smoking in the locker room. And I am like, 'This is the NBA.' And then the fighting at practice all the time. And people competed hard because the salaries weren't big, and if you were the last two or three guys and you were Black, and there was two or three white guys that were there, those three Black guys were gone.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on the unprofessional locker room culture of his rookie team
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins shares a wild story about his rookie season, where teammates were literally smoking cigarettes in the locker room.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: We in the locker room and dude pulls out a cigarette, starts smoking in the locker room.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: They weren't going to have an all-Black team. The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggaboggers. And then you know who changed the whole climate was Red Auerbach because he started five Blacks with the Boston Celtics. He didn't win everybody over because they were winning, it just happened that over time that they did. But, those types of things and I got called the N-word by my own fans. And this is a story I tell it because of the times, I am not telling it because I am proud of it.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on the racial dynamics of his early NBA teams
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins reflects on the racial climate of the NBA in his early playing days, discussing the challenges he faced from fans and the league culture.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggaboggers.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: I used to get booed because everybody I was starting in place of a veteran white guy. And he was a nice guy, he was a good guy, he wasn't me. You know, he didn't bring the juice that could help us win like that, but he was a big part of us winning the championship. And so, one night, man, they are booing me like crazy. I can't make a shot, I done turned the ball over two or three times, right? I am down on myself already. I didn't need their help.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on being booed as a rookie starting over a veteran
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins opens up about the pressure of being a rookie starting over a veteran and the harsh reaction he received from home fans.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: I used to get booed because everybody I was starting in place of a veteran white guy.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: Remember 1968 Olympics, George Foreman wins the championship in boxing. He win, pull out two little American flags, walk to center ring, put them up over his head and he bowed to every section, right? And everybody went crazy. Well, my moment was I went to center court and I put up the finger and I bowed to every section, right? And then walked to the bench. You know, you know how different that would have been now. I probably would have been suspended four or five games or something like that and the media would have been talking about it for a month.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on his defiant reaction to being booed by fans
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins recalls the time he flipped off the crowd and bowed to every section after being booed, noting he would be suspended for weeks if he did it today.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: My moment was I went to center court and I put up the finger and I bowed.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: Every practice was competitive. We didn't watch film, we didn't walk through, we practiced, we scrimmaged and we got after it. And you know, you had to not just beat the person you were going against, but you also had to help the team you on win. See, that was more important than just numbers back then. And we had that conversation later on, you and I.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on the intense, physical nature of NBA practices
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins on the old school approach to NBA practices, where the focus was entirely on scrimmaging and physical competition rather than film study.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: Every practice was competitive. We didn't watch film, we didn't walk through, we practiced, we scrimmaged.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: He was my dog. He was my roadie, and he protected me. We were playing in New Orleans in the Superdome, and Pete Maravich elbowed me and I hit him upside the head. All of a sudden this 6-11 backup center come off the bench at me, chasing me, right? Lou intercepted him. Fight's over, right? And so, he said, 'Boy, do you know we down here in Louisiana? You can get, huh, hitting Pete Maravich like that?' Because you know Pete was a star, he was the guy. And so, I didn't know. All I knew is that he, he was trying to hurt me.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on his relationship with coach Pete Maravich
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins shares a story about getting into a physical altercation with Pete Maravich and the immediate intensity of the league back then.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: He was my dog. He was my roadie, and he protected me.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins
clips.text: And that was the difference between then. You know all this hard fouling and knocking people out there, you do that, somebody is raising, they are coming at you from the ground up. They are not waiting for somebody to grab you and point fingers, they come like you. I don't bluff. Nobody bluffed back then. When they were fighting, when they were mad, they fought. And there was some big-time fights. So, that was the times of there.
clips.news_angle: Lionel Hollins on the lack of 'bluffing' in NBA fights
clips.social_post: Lionel Hollins on the difference between eras, saying that when players fought back in the day, they were not bluffing.
clips.video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was
clips.pull_quote: Nobody bluffed back then. When they were fighting, when they were mad, they fought.

clips.speaker: Lionel Hollins

They were just toughness because they were men, they were scrapping trying to take care of their families and trying to stay in that league, you know.
